en.title: Ihram and Intention
en.desc: The pilgrim performing Umrah bathes, applies perfume, and wears the Ihram garments (an izar and rida' for men), then makes the intention to enter the rite at the Miqat. It is not permissible to pass the Miqat without Ihram.

en.title: The Talbiyah
en.desc: The pilgrim begins reciting the Talbiyah, raising his voice with it (for men), and repeats it often from the moment of Ihram until he begins the Tawaf, at which point he stops.

en.title: Tawaf Around the Ka'bah — Seven Circuits
en.desc: He circles the Ka'bah seven times in a state of purity, beginning at the Black Stone, touching it or pointing to it while saying 'Allahu Akbar,' keeping the House on his left. He should recite much remembrance and supplication, including what is said between the Yemeni Corner and the Black Stone:

en.title: Praying Two Rak'ahs Behind the Station of Ibrahim
en.desc: After finishing the Tawaf, he prays two rak'ahs behind the Station of Ibrahim if possible, reciting Surat al-Kafirun after al-Fatihah in the first rak'ah and Surat al-Ikhlas in the second.

en.title: Sa'i Between Safa and Marwah
en.desc: He goes out to Safa, climbs it, faces the Qiblah, raises his hands, says 'Allahu Akbar,' and supplicates. Then he descends to Marwah; men should walk briskly between the two green markers, completing seven circuits, the last ending at Marwah. Among what is said upon Safa and Marwah:

en.title: Shaving or Trimming the Hair
en.desc: After the Sa'i, a man shaves his entire head (which is better) or trims all of it, while a woman trims a fingertip's length from her hair. With this, the Umrah is complete.

en.title: The Day of Tarwiyah (8th of Dhul-Hijjah)
en.desc: On the morning of the eighth day, he enters Ihram for Hajj, makes the intention, and recites the Talbiyah. Then he goes out to Mina, where he prays Dhuhr, Asr, Maghrib, Isha, and Fajr, shortening the four-rak'ah prayers without combining them, and spends the night of the ninth there.

en.title: The Day of Arafah (9th of Dhul-Hijjah) — The Standing
en.desc: After sunrise, he travels to Arafah, where he prays Dhuhr and Asr shortened and combined at the earlier time. Then he devotes himself to remembrance and supplication, facing the Qiblah with hands raised, until sunset. The entire area of Arafah is a place of standing, except for the valley of Uranah.

en.title: Muzdalifah — Spending the Night
en.desc: After sunset at Arafah, he proceeds calmly to Muzdalifah, where he prays Maghrib and Isha combined at the later time, and spends the night there. He gathers the pebbles for stoning the Jamarat, prays Fajr early, then remembers Allah at al-Mash'ar al-Haram until daylight appears.

en.title: The Day of Sacrifice — Stoning Jamrat al-Aqabah
en.desc: He arrives at Mina and stones the large Jamrat al-Aqabah with seven pebbles thrown in succession, saying 'Allahu Akbar' with each pebble. He stops reciting the Talbiyah when he begins the stoning.

en.title: The Sacrificial Animal and Shaving
en.desc: After the stoning, the one performing Tamattu' or Qiran slaughters the sacrificial animal, then shaves his head or trims it (shaving is better), while a woman trims a fingertip's length. With this, the first release from Ihram occurs, making everything permissible except relations with women.

en.title: Tawaf al-Ifadah (A Pillar of Hajj)
en.desc: He goes down to Makkah and performs Tawaf al-Ifadah, seven circuits, then walks Sa'i between Safa and Marwah as the Sa'i of Hajj. With this, the second release from Ihram occurs, making everything permissible.

en.title: The Days of Tashriq — Spending the Night and Stoning
en.desc: He spends the nights of Tashriq at Mina, and stones the three Jamarat each day after the sun passes its zenith: the small one, then the middle one, then al-Aqabah, seven pebbles for each. Whoever hastens leaves after stoning on the twelfth day; whoever delays also stones on the thirteenth.

en.title: The Farewell Tawaf
en.desc: If the pilgrim wishes to leave Makkah, he makes his last act at the House the Farewell Tawaf of seven circuits. It is waived for a menstruating woman or one in postpartum bleeding.
